title: The Hidden Life Cycle of Ant Colonies
hook: Ever wondered how a single ant can build an empire?
script: Ever wondered how a single ant can build an empire? Ant colonies are eusocial superorganisms, each housing queens, workers, and seasonal winged alates. The queen continuously lays eggs, which develop into larvae, then pupae, and finally into the various castes. Sterile workers tend the brood, forage for food, and maintain the nest, while soldiers defend it. When the colony matures, thousands of winged males and females—called alates—emerge and gather for a nuptial flight. During the flight, males mate briefly then die, while a few fertilized females land, shed their wings, and start new nests. These founding queens raise the first generation of workers alone, beginning the cycle anew. Thus, from a single egg to a bustling metropolis, the ant colony’s life cycle repeats across the planet.
